capability_targets.what_it_does: Configure filters/columns for the registrant list
Register for an event (claim a place/ticket)
Look up a registration from its ticket QR/UUID at the door
Export the registrant list as CSV/Excel/PDF

exemplar.notes: Not re-run this pass -- exemplar selection (Eventbrite) and admission (MIT / Flask, commit eb90264caec7d1210959c453d1f93ad88a98e6ce) were already established and proven in the prior session per NUMBER_ONE_APP.md. capability_targets above lists only the 10 catalog capabilities actually bound to real Indico code below; the other 6 catalog capabilities (take payment, issue refund, apply discount code, send push notification, manage inventory, split payout) have no real Indico implementation to target and are named in 'unresolved' instead.

harvest_source.structural_match: Indico's registration module (indico/modules/events/registration) is a real event-ticketing system: an organiser creates a registration form, prices ticket tiers (Standard/VIP were proven live), a registrant books and pays for a place, and a PDF ticket with a scannable QR code is issued and checked at the door via the check-in API -- the same register/browse/book/pay/prove-at-the-door shape as Eventbrite, minus the payment provider itself (see unresolved).

capabilities.what_it_does: Creates a new local Indico user (User + Identity) from the signup form, or files a RegistrationRequest for admin moderation if account moderation is enabled for the instance.
Authenticates a user against the local ('indico') auth provider and starts a session; on success redirects to the page that triggered the login.

security_constraints.csrf: form has its own CSRF token, global CSRF disabled for this RH

capabilities.what_it_does: Ends the current session (multipass.logout with clear_session=True) and redirects to 'next' (if it validates) or the site index.

Searches across categories, events, contributions, sub-contributions, event notes and attachments via the configured search provider (falls back to Indico's own InternalSearch for category-only queries).

security_constraints.admin_override_enabled: restricted to admins, enforced in the query schema itself

capabilities.what_it_does: Reads (GET) or stores (POST) the set of filters and visible columns used to render the registrant list for one registration form, then returns the filtered list.

side_effects: persists the filter/column configuration for the current manager

capabilities.what_it_does: Renders the detail view of a single registration (personal data, chosen ticket tier, payment/check-in state, tags, uploaded files) for event managers.

Submits the registration form for an event: validates the submitted field data against the form's schema (including per-choice capacity), creates a real Registration row, links any matching invitation, and emails the registrant a confirmation. This is the real code path this session drove live to register 'Ada Admin' for the VIP ticket tier.

security_constraints.conditionally_requires_login: if regform.require_login is set, non-GET requests must be authenticated

capabilities.what_it_does: Looks up a registration by the UUID embedded in its ticket's QR code (checkin_secret / ticket_uuid) and returns its check-in/payment state -- the real endpoint the Check-in App calls when a door scanner reads a ticket.
Sends a real templated email (with the ticket PDF attached, if the form has tickets enabled and the registration isn't ticket-blocked) to one or more selected registrants.

side_effects: sends one real email per selected registrant via indico.core.notifications.send_email
logs 'Participants emailed' on the registration form

capabilities.what_it_does: Exports the registrant list for one registration form as a CSV file (Excel .xlsx and PDF table/book variants exist on sibling routes: RHRegistrationsExportExcel, RHRegistrationsExportPDF).

slots.trigger_on: a QR/barcode scan decodes a ticket_uuid

unresolved: take payment -- Indico's core repo defines only the PaymentPluginMixin interface (indico/modules/events/payment/plugins.py:41). No concrete subclass of it exists anywhere in this repo (grep for 'PaymentPluginMixin)' across the whole tree returns only that one definition and its one isinstance() check in util.py:25). Every real payment method (manual, PayPal, Stripe, etc.) ships in the separate 'indico-plugins' PyPI package, which is not part of this repo or this commit. This matches what we proved live in the prior session: the VIP registration's invoice came back 'Not paid' because no payment plugin was installed. Per NUMBER_ONE_APP.md step 2, this capability is left out of the capabilities list rather than assigned a fabricated payment 'variant'.

issue refund -- no refund code path exists anywhere in indico/modules/events/payment or indico/modules/events/registration. The only hit for 'refund' in either module is a hardcoded default settings string in indico/modules/events/payment/__init__.py:25 telling registrants to email the conference secretary. There is nothing to bind a route to.

apply discount code -- no discount/promo/coupon concept exists in the registration module. Grepping indico/modules/events/registration for discount|promo.?code|coupon returns nothing. Registration forms have a base_price and per-choice prices (see 'manage inventory' below) but no code-gated discount mechanism.

send push notification -- no push-notification code exists anywhere in the repo (searched for push.?notification|web.?push|fcm|apns across all .py files). Indico is a server-rendered web app with email notifications (see 'send email notification'); it has no mobile/web-push channel.

split payout -- zero matches for 'payout' anywhere in the repo. Indico has one organiser per event taking payment through one configured method; there is no marketplace-style multi-party payout mechanism to bind this to.

manage inventory -- the real capability exists and is well evidenced (per-choice 'places_limit' on registration form fields, e.g. the Standard/VIP capacity we could have set on the Ticket Tier field in the prior session; enforced in indico/modules/events/registration/fields/choices.py:163-185, 'No places left for the option'). But the only route that lets a manager modify it -- RHRegistrationFormModifyField at /event/<event_id>/manage/registration/<reg_form_id>/form/sections/<section_id>/fields/<field_id> (indico/modules/events/registration/controllers/management/fields.py:384-428) -- is PATCH/DELETE only (blueprint.py: methods=('DELETE', 'PATCH')). HARVEST_PROCESS_v2.md is explicit: 'method is GET or POST only. A harvested PUT/DELETE/PATCH silently 404s' and 'it maps onto GET/POST or it does not go in.' There is no GET/POST route that lets an existing field's places_limit be changed (POST .../form/sections/<section_id>/fields only *creates* a new field, a different action from 'manage inventory' on an existing one), so this capability does not go in rather than being bound to a route it doesn't actually describe.

journey_cap_id -- left blank. Not required by NUMBER_ONE_APP.md's deliverable list for this task (number_registry.json + trees/event-ticketing.tree.txt), and assign_numbers.py does not require it: it only resolves journey_cap_id from an (undocumented) 'journey_cap_name' field if one is present, and does nothing if it is absent. Leaving both blank costs nothing for this task's actual deliverables.

role_source -- left blank. No capability here sets 'required_role' (Indico's manager access is a per-event, per-capability permission set -- see the 'permissions' list on each management capability -- not a single named role), so there is no named role for role_source to point at.

log out -- error_contract.error_codes is empty. RHLogout (indico/modules/auth/controllers.py:140-147) has no error path in the code: it runs unconditionally for logged-in or anonymous sessions alike, and an invalid 'next' URL is silently replaced rather than rejected. DS-06 in check_form_godmode.py requires a non-empty error_codes list; leaving it empty and naming the conflict here was preferred over inventing an error Indico's own code does not raise.

engine field -- set to 'Flask' for every capability. Nothing in HARVEST_PROCESS_v2.md, GOD_MODE_RULE_HARVEST_ADMISSION.md, GOD_MODE_RULE_NUMBERING.md, NUMBER_ONE_APP.md or FORM_TEMPLATE_GODMODE_v2.json defines what this field means beyond check_form_godmode.py's CAP-07 requiring it non-blank. 'Flask' is the one thing about it I could confirm with certainty (pyproject.toml classifier 'Framework :: Flask', and every route read above is a real Flask blueprint route) rather than guess at a more specific intended meaning.

data_filename / data_shape.data_access -- left blank on every capability. Indico's real persistence is PostgreSQL via SQLAlchemy models (Registration, User, Identity, RegistrationFormField, etc. -- real tables in the 'event_registration', 'users' and 'indico' schemas), not god mode's flat-JSON-file-per-entity convention that data_filename/data_access describe. Naming a '<slug>.json' file here would misrepresent how the capability actually stores data, so it is left blank rather than invented; the real table/model is named in provenance.source_symbol and what_it_does instead.

ALLOWED_TRIGGER_TYPES gap -- 'view record detail' is really triggered by clicking a table row in the registrant list, but check_form_godmode.py's ALLOWED_TRIGGER_TYPES has no row/list-item click type (it has 'button', 'form_submit', 'page_load', 'poll', 'stream', 'device_event', 'background', 'websocket' -- the v1 vocabulary's 'row_click' does not carry over to v2). Set to 'button' as the closest available value rather than leaving it invalid; flagging the gap here rather than silently picking around it.

DS-05 (output_fields required for non-binary responses) does not fit every real Indico route: 'log in' and 'log out' succeed with a bare HTTP redirect (Location header, no JSON body to name fields from), and 'view record detail' returns server-rendered HTML (management/registration_details.html) that isn't parsed into named fields anywhere in the code. 'send email notification' succeeds via jsonify_data() with no fixed payload shape either. Left output_fields empty on these four rather than inventing field names no response actually has.
